title: Recipe 24 — Docker and Helm (packaging a daemon shape for a cluster)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “Twelve Dockerfiles, five single-binary targets, one Helm chart — and the chart branches on the spec's target, because a CLI run finishes and a daemon does not.”
beats.script: Twelve Dockerfiles, five single-binary targets, one Helm chart — and the chart branches on the spec's target, because a CLI run finishes and a daemon does not. [[pause:1.2s]] The editor opens 24 docker and helm.md now. Keep this artifact in view: it is the concrete evidence behind the behavior this beat describes.

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed starter and the recipe are never touched by a take.
beats.script: Live/ is scratch — the committed starter and the recipe are never touched by a take. [[pause:900ms]] The driver clears live slash crewhaus.yaml in the scratch workspace now, giving this take a repeatable starting point without changing the committed example.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env into this one terminal.
beats.script: Sources demos/.env into this one terminal. [[pause:1.8s]] Configured provider or platform credentials are required here, so the offline verifier checks the shape but does not execute the call. Operator-supplied demos/.env.

groups.title: Beat 1 · the daemon shape the chart deploys

beats.script: Clean before we package it. Shipping a broken spec in a reproducible image just reproduces the break. [[pause:1.5s]] No credentials are involved in this check; a clean exit confirms the local path behaves as described. Lint: clean — no findings.

beats.label: Open the emitted daemon
beats.cue: “One TypeScript entry point. The Dockerfile's job is to copy this in and run it as uid 1100 with a read-only root filesystem — nothing more.”
beats.script: One TypeScript entry point. The Dockerfile's job is to copy this in and run it as uid 1100 with a read-only root filesystem — nothing more. [[pause:1.2s]] The editor opens live slash dist slash daemon.ts now. The relevant implementation is now visible, so the claim can be inspected directly instead of taken on faith.

beats.label: Blank the values file
beats.cue: “Everything the chart needs to know about this deployment lives in one file.”
beats.script: Everything the chart needs to know about this deployment lives in one file. [[pause:900ms]] The driver clears live slash my values.yaml in the scratch workspace now, giving this take a repeatable starting point without changing the committed example.

beats.label: Type the recipe's values.yaml
beats.cue: “Target picks the templates, three replicas because a daemon scales horizontally, and every secret arrives by secretKeyRef — never as a literal.”
beats.script: Target picks the templates, three replicas because a daemon scales horizontally, and every secret arrives by secretKeyRef — never as a literal. [[pause:900ms]] Watch the driver type lines 165 through 190 of 24 docker and helm.md, rebuilding live slash my values.yaml from a known state. The slice comes from committed source, so the fresh file exactly matches the example this take is introducing.

beats.label: Read the values back
beats.cue: “Nine top-level keys, and two env vars the chart promises to inject. Hold on to that list.”
beats.script: Nine top-level keys, and two env vars the chart promises to inject. Hold on to that list. [[pause:1.5s]] This is an offline proof and should complete successfully. Target: channel · replicas: 3 · 9 keys; env the chart supplies: ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, SLACK_BOT_TOKEN.
beats.command: bun -e 'const v = Bun.YAML.parse(await Bun.file("live/my-values.yaml").text()); console.log("target:", v.target, "· replicas:", v.replicas, "· keys:", Object.keys(v).join(", ")); console.log("env the chart supplies:", v.env.map((e) => e.name).join(", "))'

verify.note: target: channel · replicas: 3 · 9 keys; env the chart supplies: ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, SLACK_BOT_TOKEN

beats.label: Ask the daemon what it actually boots on
beats.cue: “Exit 1, and three names — the chart's env block only supplies two. SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET is missing from values.yaml, and you find that here instead of in a crash-loop.”
beats.script: Exit 1, and three names — the chart's env block only supplies two. SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET is missing from values.yaml, and you find that here instead of in a crash-loop. [[pause:1.5s]] Do not treat this rejection as a broken demo; exit code 1 is the expected outcome. Deliberate non-zero exit 1: 3 check(s), 3 failed (SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN|ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). Scrubbed explicitly with env -u because the Setup group already sourced .env into this shell.
beats.command: env -u SLACK_BOT_TOKEN -u SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN crewhaus channel verify live/crewhaus.yaml --offline

verify.note: deliberate non-zero — exit 1: 3 check(s), 3 failed (SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN|ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). Scrubbed explicitly with env -u because the Setup group already sourced .env into this shell. --offline is the deterministic env-only pre-flight, no network.

groups.title: One more thing · build it and render it

beats.label: Build the channel image
beats.cue: [manual] “Wraps docker buildx with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH pinned to the spec's commit, so the same source gives the same digest — and records it in docker/digests.json.”
beats.script: Wraps docker buildx with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH pinned to the spec's commit, so the same source gives the same digest — and records it in docker/digests.json. [[pause:1.8s]] This step hands control to the operator for the interactive portion. Needs a running Docker daemon and a network pull of oven/bun:1.2-alpine (the recipe's own prerequisite). Never executed by drivers:verify.

beats.label: Render the chart against those values
beats.cue: [manual] “helm template is the offline half of helm install — it shows you the Deployment, Service and Ingress the chart would create for a daemon shape.”
beats.script: Helm template is the offline half of helm install — it shows you the Deployment, Service and Ingress the chart would create for a daemon shape. [[pause:1.8s]] This is the hands-on portion of the take, so the operator completes it while the driver keeps the context visible. Needs helm on PATH plus a sibling factory checkout (../../../../factory from this driver dir). The demos CI clones factory but installs no helm, so this is never executed.

verify.note: needs helm on PATH plus a sibling factory checkout (../../../../factory from this driver dir). The demos CI clones factory but installs no helm, so this is never executed.
